```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


```{r}
library(Matrix)
library(dplyr)

setwd("~/Desktop")

# Load raw 10X data
mat <- readMM("lar1/matrix.mtx")
genes_tsv <- read.table("lar1/genes.tsv", sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
barcodes_tsv <- read.table("lar1/barcodes.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

rownames(mat) <- genes_tsv$V2
colnames(mat) <- barcodes_tsv$V1

cat("Loaded:", nrow(mat), "genes x", ncol(mat), "cells\n")
```



```{r}
# Create gene_data folder
dir.create("gene_data_new", showWarnings = FALSE)

gene_names <- rownames(mat)
cell_barcodes <- colnames(mat)
total_genes <- length(gene_names)

cat("Generating", total_genes, "gene files...\n")

for (i in seq_along(gene_names)) {
  gene <- gene_names[i]
  
  gene_df <- data.frame(
    cell_barcode = cell_barcodes,
    expression = as.numeric(mat[i, ])
  )
  
  safe_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", gene)
  write.csv(gene_df, paste0("gene_data_new/", safe_name, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
  if (i %% 2000 == 0) {
    cat("  Progress:", i, "/", total_genes, "\n")
  }
}

cat("Done! Generated", total_genes, "files\n")
```
```{r}
gene_list <- data.frame(gene = rownames(mat))
write.csv(gene_list, "gene_list_new.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved gene_list_new.csv with", nrow(gene_list), "genes\n")
```
